page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ce4.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute instance belonging to the High Clock Speed family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with hyperthreading on an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor operating at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 33 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware instruction extensions such as AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16), AES, and BMI2. The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent data, and provides a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps without hardware GPU acceleration.

The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, delivering an allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmark evaluations show balanced computational throughput, scoring 1248.0 in Geekbench single-core and 4693.0 in multi-core routines. Raw compute testing via stress-ng achieved 1576.19 in single-core and 8311.36 in multi-core workloads. While cached small-block memory throughput reaches 465.3 GB/sec, uncached read-only large-block bandwidth is limited to 37.76 GB/sec, placing memory-intensive benchmarks like PassMark memory (1739.71) and database operations (2270.53) in lower percentiles.

With its 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the ecs.ce4.2xlarge serves configurations requiring large working memory sets combined with steady dedicated CPU clock speeds. It handles Redis workloads effectively, recording 8.03 million SET operations per second, alongside steady static web serving at 7.57 GB/sec. However, larger AI inference tasks, such as medium 7B model generation at 5.5 tokens per second, demonstrate significant limits without dedicated accelerator hardware. Suitable deployments include in-memory caches, compilation pipelines, batch processing, and memory-intensive enterprise middleware.
